questions.q: What is the repeatable method this lesson describes for troubleshooting a P2P symptom?
options: Memorize every possible error message in advance
Immediately escalate every issue to Oracle support
Always assume the requester made an error
Identify the specific document in question, find its current status, and walk the chain of document numbers to locate the checkpoint that has not resolved cleanly
questions.explain: The method is to identify the document, check its status, and trace the chain back to find where it diverged from the clean path.

questions.q: A requester reports their requisition has been "stuck" for three days, and its status shows Pending Approval. What is the most likely explanation?
options: It is most likely sitting in an approver's worklist, waiting for action
The requisition was deleted
The item is out of stock at the supplier
The requisitioning business unit was deleted
questions.explain: A requisition still showing Pending Approval is typically just waiting in an approver's queue, consistent with the approval mechanics covered in lesson 7.

questions.q: An AP processor reports an invoice will not pay, and it has a matching hold. What should be checked first?
options: Whether the requester's manager approved the original requisition
Whether the invoiced quantity or price actually differs from what was ordered on the purchase order or received on the receipt
Whether the supplier's address is spelled correctly
Whether the purchase order was communicated by email or fax
questions.explain: A matching hold means the invoice fell outside tolerance against the PO and/or receipt, so comparing invoiced quantity/price to ordered/received quantity/price is the first check.

questions.q: If an invoice has no matching hold but still will not pay, what else should be checked?
options: Nothing further - an invoice with no matching hold always pays automatically
Whether the receiving clerk has the correct job role
Other validation holds, such as a tax calculation issue or an incomplete distribution
Whether the item was ever added to a catalog
questions.explain: Validation checks for holds beyond matching, such as tax or incomplete distributions, which can also block an invoice from being paid.

questions.q: During a lingering-accrual investigation, what should be checked if an invoice for the receipt does exist but has not been accounted?
options: Nothing - an existing invoice always means the accrual is fine as is
Whether that invoice is stuck on a hold somewhere, which loops back to the invoice-troubleshooting checklist
Whether the original requisition was ever approved
Whether the supplier's catalog price has changed
questions.explain: An invoice that exists but has not been accounted is often stuck on a hold, which connects this scenario back to the invoice-troubleshooting method.
